provenance.method: original Renance summaries keyed to the official NERDC JSS1 Civic Education first-term scheme

topics.title: Meaning of civic education
topics.content:
Civic education is the study of the rights, duties and responsibilities of a citizen. It teaches us how to live together peacefully and how to play our part in making our community and country better.

Why we study civic education:
- It helps us know our rights, for example the right to education.
- It teaches us our duties, for example obeying the law and paying taxes.
- It builds good values like honesty, respect and hard work.
- It prepares us to take part in the affairs of our community and country.
- It helps us understand how government works.

A citizen is a legal member of a country. Citizenship can come by birth, by registration or by naturalization (living in a country for a long time and being accepted).

Evaluation questions:
1. Define civic education.
2. Mention four reasons why civic education is important.
3. Who is a citizen?

topics.title: Rights and duties of a citizen
topics.content:
Rights are what every citizen is allowed to enjoy by law. Duties are what the citizen must do for the country.

Some rights of a Nigerian citizen:
- Right to life.
- Right to education.
- Right to personal liberty (freedom).
- Right to freedom of movement.
- Right to freedom of speech.
- Right to fair hearing in court.

Some duties of a citizen:
- Obey the laws of the land.
- Pay taxes and rates.
- Vote in elections when qualified.
- Protect public property.
- Report crime and help the security agents.
- Serve Nigeria when called upon, for example the NYSC for graduates.

Rights and duties go together. You enjoy your rights better when everyone performs their duties.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the difference between a right and a duty?
2. Mention five rights of a citizen.
3. Mention four duties of a citizen.

topics.title: National values: honesty
topics.content:
Values are the good ways of behaving that our society accepts. Honesty means being truthful and fair in everything we do.

An honest person:
- Tells the truth at all times.
- Does not take what does not belong to him or her.
- Returns things found to the owner.
- Does not cheat in examinations.
- Keeps promises.

Benefits of honesty: people trust you, you enjoy peace of mind, your school and family are proud of you, and you help the society to grow.

Dishonesty is telling lies, stealing, cheating and pretending. It brings shame, punishment and loss of trust.

Evaluation questions:
1. Define honesty.
2. Mention four qualities of an honest person.
3. State three benefits of honesty.

topics.title: Cooperation
topics.content:
Cooperation means working together with other people to achieve a common goal.

Examples of cooperation: members of a family sharing house work, students cleaning their classroom together, a football team passing the ball, neighbours contributing money for a community project.

Attributes of cooperation:
- Sharing responsibilities fairly.
- Listening to other people's ideas.
- Tolerance and patience.
- Trust and honesty among members.
- Team spirit.

Benefits of cooperation: work is finished faster, the burden is shared, members learn from one another, and peace grows in the community.

Evaluation questions:
1. Define cooperation.
2. Mention four attributes of cooperation.
3. Give three examples of cooperation at home, in school and in the community.
